item.title: Keychains
item.description:
In Layer5 Cloud, a collection of permissions is represented as a keychain. One or more keychains can are grouped together and assigned to a role. Later, a role can be assigned to a user. This is the general flow of how keychains are assigned to a user.

For instance, consider a system shipped default keychain Team Management, which is a collection of eight keys: View All Teams, Add User to Team, Invite User to Team, Remove User from Team, Create Team, Delete Team, Remove User Role from Team, and Assign User Role in a Team. This implies that you can perform all these operations only if your user account possesses a role to which Team Management keychain is assigned in a given organization.

item.title: Permissions by Role
item.description:
This page tells you which Kanvas actions require a permission, which default roles grant each permission, and which actions are limited by something other than a permission. Use it to find out why an action is missing for a user and which role grants it.

How permissions work 🔗

A permission is a named key, such as Deploy Design, that allows one action. Keys are grouped into keychains, and a role bundles one or more keychains. Your organization assigns roles to users. Before Kanvas offers certain actions, it checks whether the user holds the matching key. Kanvas uses the shared Layer5 permission set and defines no permissions of its own. See Roles and Keychains.
